adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — Making getShortcut abstract breaks every already-deployed third-party grant factory with an AbstractMethodError during encoder post-init, preventing server startup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface adds a new abstract method `getShortcut()` (lines 30-34 in the interface file). This is a breaking change for any existing third-party implementations of OAuth2GrantTypeFactory that don't implement this new method. When DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() iterates over all OAuth2GrantType provider factories and calls getShortcut() on each one (visible in the factory code), any third-party implementation without this method will throw AbstractMethodError at runtime, preventing server startup. This is a real backward compatibility bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:74 — Grant shortcuts are neither required to be non-null nor exactly two characters, so a malformed extension can either abort initialization or mint IDs that this decoder rejects.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), the code iterates over OAuth2GrantTypeFactory instances and calls gtf.getShortcut() without any validation. The OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface adds getShortcut() method but there's no enforcement that implementations return non-null or exactly 2-character strings. The encoding/decoding logic in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider assumes exactly 2 characters per component (lines 73-77 check encodedContext.length() != 6, expecting 2+2+2 chars). If a grant factory returns null or wrong-length shortcut, it would either cause NPE when putting into maps, or create token IDs that fail decoding. This is a real validation gap - the code trusts external implementations without validation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — Adding an abstract SPI method makes previously deployed OAuth2 grant factories throw AbstractMethodError during provider initialization.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `getShortcut()` is added as a new abstract method to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (line 33-37). This is an SPI (Service Provider Interface) that third-party implementations can extend. Adding a new abstract method to an interface without a default implementation is a breaking change - any existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations that were compiled against the old interface will throw AbstractMethodError at runtime when Keycloak tries to call getShortcut() on them. The built-in implementations (AuthorizationCodeGrantTypeFactory, ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory, etc.) all add the method, but external/custom implementations would break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:102 — Removing the public Context(Context) constructor breaks existing grant extensions that copy the request context at runtime.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the removal of the copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` (lines 102-115 in the old code). This constructor was previously available for external code to copy a Context object. If any existing OAuth2GrantType extensions relied on this constructor to create copies of the context (e.g., for delegation or modification), they would break at runtime with a NoSuchMethodError. The removal of a public API method is a breaking change that could affect existing implementations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — The decoder requires a two-character grant shortcut although the factory SPI neither specifies nor validates that constraint, so a valid custom shortcut can produce undecodable token IDs.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is valid. In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74, the decoder expects exactly 6 characters for encodedContext (line 74: `if (encodedContext.length() != 6)`), with characters 4-6 being the grant type shortcut (2 chars). However, the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface (line 30-34 in the diff) only specifies that getShortcut() should return a shortcut but does not enforce or validate that it must be exactly 2 characters. A custom grant implementation could return a shortcut of different length (e.g., 1 or 3 characters), which would cause the encoding to produce token IDs that cannot be properly decoded, as the decoder strictly expects 2-character shortcuts at positions 4-5.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 — The constructor never rejects a null rawTokenId, allowing encodeTokenId to emit an invalid literal `:null` identifier.

testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — isAccessTokenId uses a shifted substring and rejects matching values, so it does not actually verify the expected grant shortcut and grant-type regressions pass.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the isAccessTokenId method in the diff (lines 476-489), the substring extraction `items[0].substring(3, 5)` is incorrect. Based on the token format shown elsewhere in the diff (e.g., 'trltcc:1234' where 'tr' is session type at 0-2, 'lt' is token type at 2-4, 'cc' is grant type at 4-6), the grant shortcut should be at positions 4-6, not 3-5. Additionally, the condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` has inverted logic - it returns false when the grant MATCHES, which is backwards. This means the matcher will reject valid tokens and accept invalid ones, causing grant-type verification to not work correctly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — Adding an abstract method makes every existing custom grant factory fail during default encoder post-init instead of allowing a compatibility fallback.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `getShortcut()` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (line 33). adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:105 — Removing the public Context copy constructor is an unnecessary source and binary compatibility break for grant-provider extensions that clone request contexts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the removal of the public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` at lines 102-116 in OAuth2GrantType.java. This is a public API in server-spi-private, and removing it could break binary compatibility for any external grant-provider extensions that relied on cloning Context objects. While this may be intentional as part of the refactoring (the grantType field is now set in the main constructor from formParams), the finding correctly identifies a potential compatibility concern for extensions. This is a legitimate architectural/API concern, not a bug per se, but an important consideration for a public interface.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — The matcher extracts the wrong characters and rejects matching grants, so event tests can pass with an incorrect grant shortcut.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for the isAccessTokenId matcher at line 483: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` - This logic is inverted. It returns false when the grant shortcut MATCHES, but it should return false when it DOESN'T match. The correct logic should be `if (!items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Additionally, the substring indices appear wrong - based on the token format shown in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider (e.g., 'onrtna:5678' where first 2 chars are sessionType, next 2 are tokenType, next 2 are grantType), the grant shortcut should be at positions 4-6 (substring(4,6)), not 3-5. This bug means the matcher will incorrectly reject valid tokens and accept invalid ones.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:53 — The tests only parse hand-written IDs and never exercise context creation, leaving online/offline/transient, lightweight, and grant-attribute encoding unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test file DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java only tests getTokenContextFromTokenId() with hand-crafted token ID strings and encodeTokenId() round-trips. The test never calls getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(), which is the method that actually creates AccessTokenContext from real session data (determining online/offline/transient session type, lightweight token detection, and grant type from attributes). This is newly added nontrivial logic in the diff that lacks test coverage. The finding is specific and grounded in the actual test code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:40 — The test hand-builds grant maps instead of running factory postInit with registered grants, so SPI discovery, built-in shortcut registration, and collision validation are untested.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the unit test in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java manually constructs the grant maps (lines 43-49) rather than using the actual factory.postInit() method with real SPI discovery. This means the test doesn't verify: (1) that postInit correctly discovers OAuth2GrantType providers, (2) that built-in shortcuts are properly registered, or (3) that the collision validation logic (lines 79-82 in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory) works correctly. The diff shows new SPI infrastructure with collision detection that has no integration-level test coverage. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:476 — No direct matcher test covers matching and mismatching grant prefixes, leaving the new event assertion's expected grant effectively unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut)` matcher method at line 476 that validates token IDs contain an expected grant shortcut. However, looking at the test file changes, there are no unit tests added for this new matcher itself. The matcher has logic that checks `items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` but this appears to have a bug - it returns false when the grant DOES match (should likely be `!equals`). While the finding mentions 'no direct matcher test', this is a valid concern - new test utility code with non-trivial logic (substring parsing, format validation) should have its own tests to verify it works correctly, especially given the apparent logic issue in the implementation.
